title: Uniform conormal-layer vanishing over a local base for algebraic spaces
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] with unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, put $k=A/\mathfrak m$, and let $g:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a proper morphism of algebraic spaces [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-trf-algebraic-space, def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed. Let $N$ be a line module on the small etale site of $Z$, meaning a module sheaf locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_Z$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-trf-algebraic-space]. Put $J=\mathfrak m\mathcal O_Z$, the ideal generated by the images of the elements of $\mathfrak m$ under $g^\sharp$. Products and quotients are sheaf products and cokernels, with $J^0=\mathcal O_Z$; $J^nN$ is the submodule locally generated by products of $n$ sections of $J$ and one of $N$. Cohomology means right derived global sections of the underlying additive sheaf on $Z_{\mathrm{et}}$, and $\Gamma$ means its global sections [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $i:Z_0=Z\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}k\to Z$ be the closed fibre [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Pullback is tensor pullback in the canonical ringed etale topoi [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model]. Assume $Z_0$ is a scheme and the ordinary invertible module corresponding to $i^*N$ is ample [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence, def-sc-invertible-module, def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Tensor powers and products are those of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], with $N^{\otimes0}=\mathcal O_Z$. There exists an integer $d_0\geq0$ such that for all integers $n\geq0$ and $d\geq d_0$,
$$H^1\bigl(Z,(J^n/J^{n+1})\otimes_{\mathcal O_Z}N^{\otimes d}\bigr)=0.$$

source.place: Tag 0D39 (lemma-ample-on-fibre), proof, graded-module paragraph and the second displayed vanishing, with F = O_Z and p = 1. This is the conormal-layer input before the short exact sequences, not the section-lifting conclusion.

proof.text: Write $g_0:Z_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. The quotient $k$ is Noetherian: lift an ideal to $A$ and reduce a finite generating set modulo $\mathfrak m$. By [lem-sfb-space-proper-base-change], $g_0$ is proper in the sense of [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Since $Z_0$ and $\operatorname{Spec}k$ are schemes, this is ordinary scheme properness [def-weil-proper-morphism]: the diagonal conditions agree; the chart test for local finite type includes the identity charts; quasi-compactness tested on the affine target $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is compactness of $|Z_0|$; and for a scheme the atlas topology of [def-a1-space-point-topology] is the Zariski topology (etale maps are open, and the identity is a chart), so closedness after every scheme base change is the scheme condition. On every affine etale chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\to Z$, its closed fibre is $\operatorname{Spec}(R\otimes_Ak)=\operatorname{Spec}(R/\mathfrak mR)$. The quotient-spectrum lemma [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-closed-immersion] makes this a closed immersion. The same calculation after any scheme test, on affine opens of that test, shows that $i$ is representable by closed immersions and affine [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Its ideal is $J$, since the kernel on these charts is precisely $\mathfrak mR$.

source.place: Tag 0D39 (lemma-ample-on-fibre), proof, local base and closed-fibre setup.

proof.text: Choose generators $a_1,\ldots,a_r$ of $\mathfrak m$. The ideal $J^n$ is the image of the finite free module whose basis is the words of length $n$ in these generators, mapped to their products; for $n=0$ use the empty word and $\mathcal O_Z$. Thus $J^n$ and $Q_n=J^n/J^{n+1}$ are quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits]. On an affine etale chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$, these modules correspond to $(\mathfrak mR)^n$ and $(\mathfrak mR)^n/(\mathfrak mR)^{n+1}$: apply [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections] on $U$ and the scheme etale/Zariski equivalence [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence]. Restriction to a chart is restriction of the ringed site [lem-trf-space-enlarged-etale-ringed-site-model], so these computations concern the stated sheaf products and cokernels. We have $JQ_n=0$. The essential-image assertion of [lem-sfb-space-closed-immersion-quasi-coherent-modules] therefore gives $Q_n=i_*G_n$ with $G_n$ quasi-coherent on $Z_0$, and full faithfulness gives unique descended maps. In particular $G_0=\mathcal O_{Z_0}$.

source.place: Tag 0D39 (lemma-ample-on-fibre), graded-module paragraph; Tags 03M1, 04CJ, and 01I8/01IC for chart calculations.

proof.text: Set $B=\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m}(A)=\bigoplus_{r\geq0}\mathfrak m^r/\mathfrak m^{r+1}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring-structure], multiplication of representatives makes this a commutative graded $k$-algebra with $B_0=k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-associated-graded-finite-type], it is a finitely generated $k$-algebra, because $\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated. Put $\mathcal B=g_0^*\widetilde B$ on the scheme $Z_0$.

source.place: Tag 0D39 (lemma-ample-on-fibre), paragraph beginning Let B; algebra.tex Tag 05GH (lemma-completion-Noetherian), degree-one generation.

proof.text: Regard $G_n$ as ordinary scheme modules by [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence]. The direct sum $G=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}G_n$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits], applied on the scheme, and that equivalence preserves coproducts by their universal property. A class $a\in B_r$ acts by $b\bmod J^{n+1}\mapsto g^\sharp(a)b\bmod J^{n+r+1}$. Changing the representative of $a$ adds a product in $J^{n+r+1}$, as does changing that of $b$; hence the formula is well-defined. Multiplication, addition and the unit identities follow from multiplication of representatives. The formulas commute with restriction and descend uniquely from the $Q_n$ to the $G_n$ by full faithfulness in [lem-sfb-space-closed-immersion-quasi-coherent-modules]. They are $\mathcal O_{Z_0}$-linear and normalized on $B_0=k$, hence extend by scalar multiplication to a graded $\mathcal B$-action. The resulting map $\mathcal B\to G$, $b\mapsto b\cdot1$, is surjective: on each affine etale chart, $(\mathfrak mR)^n=\mathfrak m^nR$, so each class is a finite sum of $R/\mathfrak mR$-multiples of images of classes in $B_n$. Consequently $G$ is a finite type graded $\mathcal B$-module, generated by the single degree-zero section $1$.

source.place: Tag 0D39 (lemma-ample-on-fibre), finite type graded module generated in degree zero; explicit representative action and generation.

proof.text: Let $L$ be the ordinary invertible module corresponding to $i^*N$; it is ample by hypothesis. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-formal-systems-graded-vanishing] over the Noetherian ring $k$ to the proper scheme $g_0$, the finitely generated graded algebra $B$, and the finite type graded module $G$. Choose its bound increased to $d_0\geq0$. Then $H^1(Z_0,G\otimes L^{\otimes d})=0$ for every $d\geq d_0$. For each $n$, the inclusion and projection $G_n\to G\to G_n$ compose to the identity. After tensoring and applying the cohomology functor, their composite is still the identity, so $H^1(Z_0,G_n\otimes L^{\otimes d})=0$. This is a retract argument, requiring no commutation of cohomology with an infinite sum. By [lem-sc-etale-zariski-qcoh-comparison], this is also vanishing of the underlying additive etale sheaf. The tensor with $L^{\otimes d}$ is quasi-coherent because on a frame it is just $G_n$. The scheme equivalence identifies its etale version with $G_n\otimes(i^*N)^{\otimes d}$: in local frames the comparison sends $x\otimes e^{\otimes d}$ to the same tensor, and on overlaps both maps multiply by the same $d$-th power of the frame-change unit.

source.place: Tag 0D39 (lemma-ample-on-fibre), first displayed vanishing; Tag 0897 (coherent-lemma-graded-finiteness)(2), Tag 03DW (descent-proposition-same-cohomology-quasi-coherent)(2).

proof.text: For each $n,d$, there is an isomorphism $Q_n\otimes N^{\otimes d}\simeq i_*(G_n\otimes(i^*N)^{\otimes d})$. Indeed, on a frame $e$ of $N$, both sides identify with $Q_n=i_*G_n$, by $x\otimes e^{\otimes d}\mapsto x$ and its pulled-back frame on $Z_0$. If $e'=ue$, both identifications change by multiplication by $u^d$ (by $i^\sharp(u)^d$ before pushforward), which is the same action on $i_*G_n$. These local isomorphisms therefore glue, also for $d=0$. The canonical ringed-site model lets us check this on etale frames, and the direct-image definition gives the indicated scalar action. This proves the required instance of the projection formula directly from a line frame.

source.place: Tag 0D39 (lemma-ample-on-fibre), comparison before the second displayed vanishing; projection formula for a line module, written on frames.

proof.text: The closed immersion $i$ is affine by step 1. Apply [lem-sfb-space-affine-cohomology] to the quasi-coherent module $G_n\otimes(i^*N)^{\otimes d}$ on $Z_0$. Its edge isomorphism and step 6 identify $H^1(Z,Q_n\otimes N^{\otimes d})$ with $H^1(Z_{0,\mathrm{et}},G_n\otimes(i^*N)^{\otimes d})$. The latter group vanishes by step 5. The same $d_0$ works for every $n\geq0$ and $d\geq d_0$, which is the assertion.

lean.note: The schematic closed fibre is any representative of the actual presheaf pullback square. Its ordinary line is restriction of canonical tensor pullback to Zariski opens. Conormal layers are kernels of successive existing base-ideal quotient maps, computed on the existing equivalent small affine etale model, which also carries the sheaf tensor and additive Sheaf.H.
